data.description:
## Symptom

Closing `cb2b-7446-748c-47bc` through the MCP `transition_ticket` tool failed with
`completion verification FAILED — 5 unmet criteria; not closing`, for work that was **already
merged** as `e21f3240cd0` and whose 5 ACs had all been re-verified green on the landed tree
minutes earlier.

The findings were not vague. They cited exact symbols at exact line numbers:

> `_ALIASES` is still defined at `src/rebar/_config_sections.py:200` and the alias loop at
> lines 246-252 still iterates over it. [...] The tombstone registry at
> `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:130-172` still contains 19 rows (6 error + 13 warn), not 6.

Every one of those statements is true — **of a tree that is not the one being closed**.

## Root cause

The rebar MCP server process runs with its working directory at the repo root
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`. Completion verification defaults its tree source to that
process's HEAD. That checkout was parked on an unrelated side commit, `2e28d817a7e`
("Annotate the unannotated library facade params"), which predates the change:

```
$ git -C /Users/joeoakhart/rebar rev-parse HEAD
2e28d817a7eefca3935a0ead4c84d584eda8c201
$ grep -n '^_ALIASES' src/rebar/_config_sections.py
200:_ALIASES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor e21f3240cd0 HEAD && echo ancestor || echo NOT
NOT
```

Line 200 is exactly the line the verifier cited. The agent's work was in a linked worktree at
`.rebar/worktrees/impl-cb2b`, correctly at `e21f3240cd0`. The verifier never saw it.

## Why this is worse than an ordinary false negative

1. **The findings are maximally convincing.** Specific symbols, specific line numbers,
   internally consistent, and individually checkable — against the wrong tree. An agent that
   trusts them will conclude the implementation was never written and re-implement landed work,
   or worse, "fix" a tree that is already correct.
2. **It contradicts the workflow the guidance mandates.** `AGENTS.md` directs agents to work in
   a fresh worktree *and* to route tracker operations through the MCP server. Those two
   instructions together produce this failure as the default path, not as an edge case.
3. **The close precheck passes while the verifier fails.** The precheck looks for a
   trailer-bearing commit reachable from HEAD and is satisfied, so the two halves of the same
   gate disagree about which tree is under consideration.
4. **Nothing in the output names a ref.** The failure message contains no SHA, no branch, and
   no path for the tree that was read. There is no way to tell a genuine unmet criterion from a
   wrong-tree read by reading the message.

`4217-7ee6-a22b-4507` (invocation-consistent git-rev pinning) does **not** cover this. It
addresses re-resolving a symbolic ref more than once *within* one operation, and its caveat 2
explicitly assumes "library/MCP callers thread `ref` explicitly (or `None` for lazy)". This bug
is about what the lazy default *means* when the server process is a different checkout from the
caller's worktree.

## Workaround that worked

Pass the landed SHA explicitly: `verify_completion_start(ticket, ref="e21f3240cd0")`, then
`transition_ticket(..., ref="e21f3240cd0")`. This is correct behavior of a documented
parameter, not a bypass — but it only helps an agent who has already diagnosed the trap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 A completion-verification FAIL reports the concrete tree it read — the resolved
      40-char SHA and its source (`HEAD` of which path, or the explicit `ref`) — in the failure
      message itself, so wrong-tree reads are distinguishable from genuine unmet criteria
      without re-deriving them. Proven by a test asserting the SHA appears in the FAIL output.
- [ ] AC2 When the resolved verification tree does **not** contain the trailer-bearing commit
      that the close precheck accepted, the operation reports that mismatch explicitly rather
      than emitting per-criterion findings. The two halves of the gate must not disagree
      silently about which tree is under consideration. Proven by a test that sets the server
      tree and the precheck-satisfying commit to different, non-ancestor revisions.
- [ ] AC3 `git grep -nE 'verif(y|ication)' -- docs/plan-review-gate.md` surfaces a passage
      stating that over MCP the default tree is the **server process's** checkout, not the
      caller's worktree, and naming `ref` as the way to target the landed commit.
- [ ] AC4 A regression test reproduces this exact shape: ticket closed from worktree W at
      commit C, server checkout at commit D where C is not an ancestor of D, and asserts the
      run does not produce per-criterion "not implemented" findings sourced from D.
- [ ] AC5 `make verify` green.

## Notes

Severity rests on the combination of a wrong answer, high confidence, and a default path that
the project's own guidance steers agents onto. The fix need not change which tree is read by
default — naming the tree and refusing on a precheck/verifier tree mismatch would be enough to
make the failure self-diagnosing.
data.title: Completion-gated close over MCP verifies the SERVER checkout's HEAD, not the agent's worktree, and reports confident line-cited FAILs for landed work
